One row per model or configuration: the dot is the estimate, the line its interval.
The grey row is the reference.
Every row shares one axis, so their positions compare directly.
Lowest: second variant model (Explainable Boosting Machine) at . Highest: mean baseline at .
Two overlapping lines do not prove two models equal when they were measured on the same rows: their paired difference decides.
The dot is the difference; the line is its interval.
The vertical line marks zero: no difference at all.
The side of zero says which one is ahead; an interval across zero says these rows cannot tell.
linear model − mean baseline: , entirely below zero.
An interval that includes zero does not prove there is no difference; it says these rows cannot tell.

Each point is the value of one group; the line around it is its interval.
The grey band is what chance alone draws for groups of that size: a point outside it suggests a real difference.
A hollow point has too few rows to be read alone.
One bar per group: to the right of zero, the model predicts too low on average in that group; to the left, too high.
A hatched bar has too few rows to be read alone.
Highest: 81 to 82 year (19xx) (). Lowest: 73 to 75 year (19xx) ().
Hunting through many groupings for one that shows something multiplies the chances of a pattern due to chance.
Draft only: nothing was recorded. Proposing creates a proposal, not a decision.

Adopt the linear model. On the out-of-fold predictions of the 318 development rows its mean absolute error is 3.69 mpg against 7.16 for the mean (paired difference -3.47, interval -3.97 to -2.96). These predictions were used to choose, so the figures are development evidence and optimistic.
Chosen by the junior in the companion's What if? view (result 5cb4ede7).

: the observed value minus the predicted one; positive, the model predicted too low
Median residual -0.15; the middle half lies between -3.01 and 2.69.
A mean residual near zero in every group means the model errs in both directions as often; a group far from zero is predicted too high or too low as a whole.
A mean residual near zero does not mean small errors: errors in both directions cancel out. Read it with the mean absolute error of the group.
Where the residuals lean, the model leans.
